court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court at Bombay, Family Court Appeal No. 48 of 2008
case_name: Nanda Shamkant Kanade vs Shamkant Sadashiv Kanade
facts_of_case: Marriage between parties was solemnized in 1989. Parties have been residing separately since 2004. Petitioner-husband filed petition for divorce on grounds of cruelty and desertion. Trial court allowed the petition and granted decree of divorce.

legal_principles.principle: Burden lies on the party making allegations to establish them.
legal_principles.held: The allegations made in paragraph-11 of the written statement were not put to the respondent in his cross-examination to enable him to explain the same.
cited_cases: Nanda Shamkant Kanade vs Shamkant Sadashiv Kanade, (2016)

legal_principles.principle: A party cannot make serious allegations against the other without substantiating them.
legal_principles.held: The learned Judge recorded a finding that even the said allegations are also not proved.
cited_cases: Nanda Shamkant Kanade vs Shamkant Sadashiv Kanade, (2016)

outcome.final_order: Decree of divorce under section 13(1) (ia) of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 was upheld. Certain amounts were ordered to be paid by respondent to petitioner and minor son.

use_for_drafting: responding to a petition for divorce
